- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) and forecast is low, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid underreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), reduce forecast by 10–15% in next 3–5 days to account for mean reversion.  
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward bias correction (reduce by 2–5% per day).  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.33) and forecast is erratic, smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is below 65 and forecast is above 70, apply downward correction to align with recent mean.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “+0.67” followed by “-0.33”, expect a downward correction in next 5–7 days.  
- When forecast is > 75 and true outcome is < 65, assume overestimation; reduce by 10–15% and apply lag correction (delayed drop).
